subject: Finalizing IP carveouts and runtime use — MSA & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@meadowcorp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Meadow Corp Procurement <procurement@meadowcorp.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — IP & runtime questions

Alex — attaching our redlines to the MSA and order form. A few of the items we need clarity on before procurement can move to signature: 

1) Output ownership: Meadow intends to own outputs produced by the Service when our prompts/corp data are used to generate content. We flagged assignment language in the order form but legal marked it for your review.

2) Training / model retrain: we require explicit opt-in if Redwood will use any Meadow content (prompts, outputs, or telemetry) to further train models. Please confirm mechanisms (export, deletion, opt-out).

3) Feedback license: our product team wants an explicit carveout for telemetry and aggregated usage, but we need a clear non-training clause or a controlled license.

4) Productization concern: we cannot assign output rights that enable Redwood to resell derivatives of our proprietary data.

We noted two proposed attachment items (evidence of SOC2, sample telemetry logs retention policy). Procurement would like a proposed path forward in writing by EOD tomorrow so we can get legal alignment.

Attachments: MeadowCorp_MSA_OrderForm_REDLINE_20270630.docx

Thanks,

Sara Lowe
Senior Sourcing Manager, Meadow Corp
procurement@meadowcorp.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@meadowcorp.com>
Cc: Meadow Corp GC <legal@meadowcorp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — IP & runtime questions

Sara — thanks for the clear redlines. High level response and proposed path: 

- Output ownership: Redwood is comfortable with customers retaining ownership of customer-provided content and the direct outputs of the service (i.e., text/images generated from their prompts). We will propose explicit order-form language that assigns title to Meadow for outputs created from Meadow inputs.

- Training / retrain: we can agree that Redwood will not use Meadow prompts/outputs to train or improve any public models without explicit, opt-in written consent. For operations, we do collect telemetry and aggregated metrics to run the service; we propose a narrow "feedback" license limited to operational improvements (bug fixes, performance tuning) that expressly excludes training new models.

- Productization: we will add a prohibition on using Meadow outputs to create a competing product or to commercialize Meadow-origin content outside the service, and we can include a representation/waiver for downstream distribution if that helps.

- Evidence items: happy to share SOC2 report and a one-page telemetry retention summary.

Attached: Redline_Summary_ProposedLang.txt — contains tracked-propose snippets (Order Form Exhibit A language for assignment; MSA Section 5.x for feedback license).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Laura and I will draft precise contract text by end of day.
2) Quick 30-min legal call tomorrow to walk GC through the changes (we can host).
3) Procurement confirms target sign date by next Friday so we can schedule COE and provisioning.

If this aligns I'll schedule the legal sync and circulate a calendar invite.

Best,

Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

Attachments: Redline_Summary_ProposedLang.txt

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — IP & runtime questions

Alex / Dev — drafting notes for the call and proposed contract language. Summary of recommended positions (legal):

- Keep the Order Form assignment for "Outputs" but limit definition of "Outputs" to content generated by the Service that contains or is derived from Customer Input. Add an express exclusion for pre-existing Redwood models and baseline model weights.

- Add a "Training Exclusion" clause to the MSA: "Redwood will not use Customer Input, Customer Outputs, or customer-provided telemetry to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update any model used to provide the Service, unless Customer provides explicit, documented consent via the Order Form or separate written agreement."

- Feedback/Operational License: propose a narrow, revocable license limited to aggregated, de-identified metadata and service telemetry for the sole purpose of improving service reliability and performance. Include a retention cap (e.g., 90 days) and deletion workflow on termination.

- Derivative claims / indemnity: suggest inserting a mutual representation that Customer has rights to deploy Customer Input and that Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer-originated Outputs; consider carveout language for third-party trademarks and licensed content.

- Escrow / evidence: when Customer requires escrow or auditability for claims of ownership, propose a constructive path — sample logs, hash commitments for outputs, and SOC2 evidence to be attached as exhibits.

I'll prepare redline snippets for the 30-minute GC call. Alex — please confirm the timing you propose to Sara and procurement. We should avoid over-indexing on productization language that could block provisioning; the language should protect Meadow without preventing standard service telemetry.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Alex / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear positions. Procurement is comfortable with the proposed templates subject to two small edits: 

1) The Training Exclusion should include an audit right (limited, on notice) to verify that data was not used for model training for a period of 12 months post-termination. We understand this can be scoped tightly (forensic hash checks, sample artifacts) — procurement will accept a narrow audit clause.

2) Feedback license: extend the retention cap to 120 days (we can be flexible if Redwood can tighten access controls and provide deletion certificates).

We can take your redline snippets in the call. I circulated the DocuSign route with our procurement queue; they indicated a final legal sync tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT would be ideal. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/MEAD-2027-034/redirect
